sections.title: Intermediate Concept: Approximation
sections.content: In 'Approximation' questions, options are spaced far apart. You round off numbers to their nearest whole integer before applying BODMAS. Example: 15.99 becomes 16; 114.03 becomes 114; 24.9% becomes 25%.

sections.title: Handling Mixed Fractions
sections.content: A mixed fraction A(b/c) is essentially A + (b/c). When adding or subtracting multiple mixed fractions, separate the whole numbers from the fractions, solve them individually, and merge them back at the end.

sections.title: Square Root Extraction (Unit Digit Method)
sections.content: Look at the last digit of the perfect square. 1 ends in 1 or 9; 4 ends in 2 or 8; 9 ends in 3 or 7; 6 ends in 4 or 6; 5 ends in 5. Ignore the last two digits, find the nearest smaller square for the remaining digits, and use the 'midpoint (5)' square to confirm the exact unit digit.

sections.title: Cube Root Extraction
sections.content: Cube roots are easier than square roots because every digit 0-9 has a unique unit digit cube mapping. (1->1, 4->4, 5->5, 6->6, 9->9). Pairs that flip: 2->8, 8->2, 3->7, 7->3. Check the unit digit, strike off the last 3 digits, and find the nearest smaller cube for the rest.

sections.title: Unit Digit Concept for Addition/Multiplication
sections.content: If the options in a simplification question all have different unit digits, do not solve the whole equation. Only calculate the unit digits of the numbers to find the answer instantly.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Converting large mixed fractions into improper fractions (huge time waste). 2. Rounding off 15.5 to 15 instead of 16. 3. Applying approximation in exact 'Simplification' questions (look at the question heading).

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 is about smart manipulation. Split mixed fractions, extract roots purely by unit digit analysis, and strictly round off decimals in approximation questions before starting any arithmetic.

tricks.title: Mixed Fraction Split
tricks.explanation: To solve 4(1/3) + 5(1/2) - 2(1/6), do not make them 13/3, 11/2 etc. Separate integers and fractions.

tricks.title: Cube Root in 3 Seconds
tricks.explanation: Find cube root of 314432. Unit digit is 2, so the root ends in 8. Strike out last 3 digits (432). Left with 314. Nearest smaller cube to 314 is 216 (6³). Answer = 68.
tricks.example: Cube root of 19683. Unit digit 3 -> ends in 7. Strike 683. Left with 19. Nearest smaller cube is 8 (2³). Answer = 27.

tricks.title: Squaring Numbers Ending in 5
tricks.explanation: To square a number ending in 5, multiply the remaining digit(s) by the next consecutive integer and attach 25 at the end.
tricks.example: 65². Multiply 6 by the next number (7). 6 x 7 = 42. Attach 25. Answer is 4225.

tricks.title: Base 100 Multiplication
tricks.explanation: To multiply numbers close to 100 (e.g., 104 x 106). Add the offsets (4+6 = 10) -> 110. Multiply the offsets (4x6 = 24). Combine them: 11024.
